name: Dead Souls 3.0
english_description: The real, self-identified 'Dead Souls' object library at its 3.0 point release (released 2009-12-30 per the archive's own doc/RELEASE_NOTES version history, signed Cratylus @ Dead Souls) -- confirmed to be a genuine, distinct point release sitting in the SAME '3.x' codebase lineage as this collection's ds386/deadsouls_fluffos (3.8.6, released 2014), NOT the dsI (1996-98 Nightmare-IV-era) or dsII (2006, 'Dead Souls II') generations. A structural and byte-level diff against ds386's own raw archive shows this is far closer to ds386 than dsII ever was: 90.8% of shared files (4136/4555) are byte-identical, master.lpc differs by only 8 trivial lines (game-balance constants, not architecture), and the domain set (campus, cave, default, examples, Praxis, town, Ylsrim -- 7 domains) is a strict subset of ds386's 9 (missing only amigara and learning, added in later 3.x releases). Not a byte-identical duplicate -- 419 shared files differ and 43 files exist only here -- so recorded as a genuinely distinct release (duplicate_of left null) rather than folded into ds386, but ported using ds386's own fix catalog wholesale since nearly every driver-compat bug (missing get_root_uid()/get_bb_uid()/creator_file(), the log_error()-during-compile recursion, a stale runtime_config.h slot-numbering mismatch, the __DIR__/__FLUFFOS__ macro collisions, the OLD_ED rewrite of lib/editor.lpc, a mistyped LIB_REMOTE path, SetLong()/SetExternalDesc()/SetInternalDesc() declared too narrowly, daemon/books.lpc's array-vs-mapping mismatch, a broken set_pre_exit_functions() call in domains/Praxis/supply2.lpc) proved to be the SAME pre-existing bugs, byte-identical down to the line, already cataloged from onboarding ds386. New findings not seen on any sibling: a mixed-encoding curse-word table (Latin-1 Finnish words plus one already-UTF-8 Cyrillic word in the same array literal, one lossy conversion actually corrupting string-literal syntax), the old-MudOS 'TYPE array NAME' dialect surviving in a handful of shapes ds386's own sweep didn't need to handle (a 'class TYPENAME array NAME' function return type, a 'TYPE array NAME1, NAME2 = default' multi-declarator-with-initializer, a bare 'array NAME = default'), and -- most notably -- a real, automatic, boot-time outbound HTTP connection: secure/daemon/autoexec.lpc (itself preloaded) schedules a call to secure/cmds/creators/dsversion.lpc's cmd() one second after every boot, which fetches doc/RELEASE_NOTES fresh from the still-live dead-souls.net over a real socket -- confirmed live (returned real 2020-era content, i.e. the site is not dead), reproducible on a bare idle boot with zero player interaction, in addition to (not instead of) the already-expected IMC2/Intermud outbound connections. 2282 of 2291 files pass a full lpcc compile sweep (99.6%); the 9 that don't are all pre-existing non-bugs (a deliberate author anti-load trap, two builder-tool scaffolding templates, a missing LIB_CAPTURE library component, a missing opcprof() efun, and 4 lpcc-batch eval-cost-budget artifacts confirmed to compile and run fine standalone/live).
